subject: title on two lines with two different colors

messages.author: 797b131071d5bc8a
messages.subject: title on two lines with two different colors
parts:
Hello every one

i want to put my title on two lines ,i can do that with this code:

     labs(title = paste("Moyenne = ", round(Moyenne.PTIME,4) ,"\t",
                       "PTIME_DELTA = ", PTIME_DELTA, "\n",
                       "Quantile.PTIME_ACTUAL_80 = ", Quantile.PTIME_ACTUAL_80)
         , aspect.ratio = 1) 

but my problem is that i want to put the first line: "Moyenne = ", round(Moyenne.PTIME,4) ,"\t", "PTIME_DELTA = ", PTIME_DELTA      in green color and the second one:
      "Quantile.PTIME_ACTUAL_80 = ", Quantile.PTIME_ACTUAL_80 in another color bule or red ....



thanks for your help

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: title on two lines with two different colors
parts:
I don't think you'd be able to do that in ggplot2 per se. Color is one
of the theme-related properties of a title and theme properties can
only be set AFAIK (i.e., set to a single value). The idiom is
something like

... + theme(plot.title = element_text(colour = "some color code or
name", size = 20, ...) + ...

where the string for colour could be a name like "brown" or a hex code
"000000" or any other supported color coding. The point is that only
one value can be passed to that element. There may be a way to do some
magic with the grid or gtable packages, but that's out of my element.
One of the gurus will have to show you if that can be done.

Dennis
